ALG_2020: Every neutralising method turns this into grey sand with a dark shoal, and that is the honest answer. With red at zero there is no colour to recover. Plain compensation (rc_gw) leaves a warm patch in the bright water, the neutral variant removes it, and CLAHE brings up the sand ripples the shoal is swimming over. MLLE's channel-exchange rule misfires and splits the frame into pink and green. Dive Color Corrector cannot get past blue because there is no red to hue-shift towards. WaterNet leaves this one blue as well.
CYM_Farm_S_2026-04-29: The dark clip, and the one that exposes the noise trade-off. Every contrast method makes the pollack easier to see against the water, but CLAHE and the unsharp mask also lift the sensor grain in the water column, which is why the final pipeline denoises first. Fusion is the smoothest but flattest. Dive Color Corrector produces blotchy blue noise, the worst result on the sheet.
CYM_Farm_S_2026-05-27: The clip that decides it: a ballan wrasse over cobble. In the original the fish is a blue smudge. Compensation alone makes it a warm grey; the neutral variant shows the wrasse's barred flank, the rubble and the mooring pipe, with the little real red this clip has kept at 70 percent. Fusion is smoother and warmer with less texture. MLLE washes out to pink and green, and Dive Color Corrector only lifts the haze while leaving the cast. WaterNet, run on the GPU, lifts contrast a little and leaves the clip blue.
ALG_SC_11: A solid green water column with a sandy floor at the bottom. With nothing neutral in frame this is the hardest case for any white balance, and the compensation methods still land on grey. The neutral variant recovers the sand ripples; fusion flattens them. MLLE blows the water out to white and Dive Color Corrector paints it sepia, the tropical-water assumption failing on UK green water.
NORF-1: The greenest clip in the archive, and the cleanest demonstration of the chroma cap. Every compensation method lands on grey because there is no red to be had, and the neutral variant is the one that brings up the shells and stones on the seabed. MLLE leaves a milky haze. Dive Color Corrector turns the whole frame mustard yellow, the failure the practitioner research predicted for green UK water. WaterNet turns the green water teal and stops there.
CYM_Control: A spider crab on gravel, blue day. The crab's legs and carapace texture come out clearly in the neutral variant, which also holds a little of this clip's real red (median 12). Plain compensation gives the pipe a yellow cast; the neutral cap removes it. MLLE splits into pink and green again, and Dive Color Corrector stays blue.
ATLMAR: One of the darkest clips: anemones and sea squirts on cobble under teal water. The neutral variant is the only one that makes the seabed fauna crisp without the haze; plain compensation and fusion stay murky because they have no local-contrast step. MLLE and Dive Color Corrector both lift the haze into a white veil across the top of the frame.
CYM_Farm_S_2026-06-02: Same Ramsey Sound site as the blue wrasse clip, six days later, on the green side of the AWB flip. The point of this pair is that both days end up in the same neutral rendering, so a spotter no longer sees two different-coloured farms. The neutral variant brings up the cobble and the crab in the foreground; fusion is softer; MLLE and Dive Color Corrector fail the same way as on the Blakeney clip.
